title: Annotatio IV §.XXIV: Clarissimus Professor’s calumny — Reformed feign belief; Danhauer’s Waldenses defense vs Mariana
pass_a_gloss: But the truth and evidence of this assertion, firmed and stabilized by as many Reformed testimonies as possible, so lately struck the eyes of a certain most Famous Professor that in a public Disputation on the Supper held by him chamber-fashion last year, in order to prove — by a certainly deplorable attempt — a fundamental Dissension of Protestants in this article, he was not ashamed to write in §. 3 that the Reformeds’ words and external Confessions do not match their Faith — i.e. to use his words: that the Reformed do not really believe what they pretend to believe, and that it is clear to everyone that they feel one thing and speak another. To which most grave injury, so unfairly inflicted on the whole Reformed Church and for so foul and invidious an end, we reply nothing else than the words of his own faithful Preceptor Joh. Conr. Danhauer, by which he defended the Waldenses’ cause in that same case against Joh. Mariana and other Pontiffs — yet to be recited by us without any application to the Professor’s Person: Still in our age, he says, the Pontiffs have dared to write that the Waldenses held Christ’s body not to be in the Eucharist sacrament. They color the matter by another calumny which the Waldenses themselves recount in the Excusing Response to Augustine’s Letters p. 87: They falsely charge us that this is not our Confession, on the ground that we write one thing about the Sacrament of Christ’s Body and believe another. These things being thus premised, Danhauer subjoins what is not alien from this place: For this is the last refuge of those who, if they were otherwise forced to swallow back their calumnies, demand hypocrisy of the adversary without reason; Dissert. on the Waldensian Church art. 4 Phenom. 10 §. 34 in the middle.
pass_b_english: A Clarissimus Professor’s public Supper Disputation lately charged that Reformed confessions do not match their faith — that they feign belief and feel one thing while speaking another (§. 3).

Strimesius answers the grave injury with Danhauer (not applied to the Professor’s person): Pontiffs once said the same of the Waldenses; the Waldenses’ excusing reply and Danhauer call hypocrisy-without-reason the calumniator’s last refuge.
source_text: Cæterùm assertionis hujus veritas ac evidentia, Reformatorum testimoniis quàm plurimis firmata ac stabilita, adeo nuper perstrinxit cujusdam Professoris Clarissimi oculos, ut in Disputatione publica de Cœna, superiori anno cameraliter ab eo habitâ, quò fundamentalem in hoc articulo Protestantium Dissensum, deplorando certè conatu, evinceret, verba Reformatorum Confessionesque externas, Fidei ipsorum non congruere, h. e. ut verbis ejus utar; Reformatos reverà id non credere quod se credere simulant, neminique non constare, aliud illos sentire, aliud loqui, haud verecundatus fuerit scribere §. 3. Cui gravissimæ injuriæ, toti Ecclesiæ Reformatæ adeo iniquè, & ob finem tam tetrum invidiosumque illatæ, nihil aliud reponimus, quàm fidi Præceptoris sui, Joh. Conr. Danhaueri verba, quibus Waldensium causam, in isto eodem casu, contra Joh. Marianam aliosque Pontificios, defendit, citra tamen omnem, ad Personam Professoris applicationem à nobis recitanda: Adhuc nostro, inquit, seculo, ausi sunt Pontificii scribere, statuisse Waldenses, in Eucharistia sacramento corpus Christi non esse. Colorem rei faciunt per aliam calumniam, quam ipsi Waldenses recensent in Responsione excusatoria ad Literas Augustin. pag. 87. Falso nos arguunt, non esse hanc nostram Confessionem, ex ejusmodi ratione, quod alia scribimus de Sacramento Corporis Christi, & alia credimus. Quibus ita præmissis, subjicit Danhauerus id, quod ab hoc loco alienum non est: Hoc nim. ultimum effugium est eorum, qui si aliàs resorbere calumnias cogerentur, hypocriseos adversarium sine ratione postulant; Dissert. de Ecclesia Waldensium. art. 4. Phænom. 10. §. 34. in medio.
